principles: Close only what is backed by runnable evidence.
Preserve the parent roadmap intent instead of replacing it with a narrower checklist.
Keep Authority Server semantics retired and out of future runtime claims.
Prefer small focused hardening over new parallel state machines.
drivers: B-43de parent roadmap rows M4-M12 are currently open.
The user explicitly wants all M4-M12 completed, not reclassified as future work.
Several implementation surfaces already exist and must be audited before adding new code.

options.name: A: close rows through evidence-backed registry and focused missing hardening
pros: Uses existing implemented surfaces where already present
Adds only missing verification needed for the parent roadmap rollup
Produces a machine-verifiable done state for B-43de
cons: May need focused doc and smoke updates across several modules

options.name: B: create separate child stories for each remaining roadmap row
cons: Slower and risks leaving the parent roadmap partially open again
Does not satisfy the current user request to finish M4-M12 now

options.name: C: update documentation status only
cons: Would repeat the original failure mode by claiming DONE without machine evidence
Would not make parent_roadmap_status close M4-M12

chosen: A: close rows through evidence-backed registry and focused missing hardening
rationale: Option A directly satisfies the user request by closing each roadmap row only when existing or newly added machine evidence proves it, while avoiding a second roadmap state machine.

preMortem.scenario: A row is marked closed by prose only.
preMortem.trigger: The document is edited without updating parent roadmap machine rows or smoke tests.
preMortem.mitigation: Require parent_roadmap_status and parent-roadmap-totality smoke evidence before marking checklist items done.

preMortem.scenario: Existing commands are counted as coverage even though they are diagnostic-only.
preMortem.trigger: Evidence mapping ignores command claim boundaries.
preMortem.mitigation: Use row notes that distinguish runtime hard gates from read-only/advisory capabilities and only claim what tests prove.

preMortem.scenario: Authority Server wording is accidentally restored as future work.
preMortem.trigger: Old roadmap sections are edited mechanically.
preMortem.consequence: Retired architecture semantics leak back into the backlog.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep Authority-facing rows retired/legacy-only and run vocabulary/doc checks while updating the roadmap.
